title: Make your own average day strip
description: A project shows how to turn the activities of many days into one average day on a strip of forty eight boxes. A made-up example of three nights of sleep shows the method, and the child then repeats it for each activity and for an adult.
teaching_notes: One idea: average each activity over the days, then double the hours for the boxes. The sleep hours in the video are a made-up example, not data.

source: Figure it Out (more on mean and median, question 12)
video_script.why: The child has made one-day strips and found an average, and now averages many days before colouring the boxes.
video_script.substitution: Add the times of each activity over the days, divide by the number of days, and double the hours for the boxes.
video_script.anchor: an activity strip of forty eight boxes, with a second strip for an adult
video_script.payoff_line: eight hours of sleep colours sixteen boxes

final_answer.value: A strip of the average day, compared with an adult's strip
final_answer.spoken: eight hours of sleep colours sixteen boxes

maths_rules: the example nights are made up to show the method: 8, 9 and 7 hours
2 boxes for each hour: 8 x 2 = 16 boxes
a full day is 24 hours x 2 = 48 boxes; the activity boxes must add to 48
the child's own readings and the adult's strip come from their own tracking; none is given
video_script.design: One idea: average each activity over the days, then double for the boxes. The wrong idea would be to colour the total of the days. The strip stays on screen all video.
open_questions: The sleep hours in the video are a made up example to show the method, not data.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This project is from your book.
<bookmark mark='strips'/>You make your own activity strip, and then one for an adult at home.
<bookmark mark='acts'/>You record sleeping, eating, studying and time outdoors for several days.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we turn many days into one average day on a strip?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko appears at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the strip with pairs of boxes bracketed as hours; the words average of the days appear

marks.day: the strip shows twenty four pairs of boxes, two boxes for each hour
marks.avg: the words average of the days appear beside the strip
marks.act: each activity gets its own colour on the strip

narration: <bookmark mark='day'/>A strip has forty eight boxes, two boxes for each hour of the day.
<bookmark mark='avg'/>An average day shares the time of many days equally.
<bookmark mark='act'/>Each activity gets its boxes from its own average hours.

beats.on_screen: Given (example only): sleep 8 h, 9 h, 7 h on three nights; 1 hour = 2 boxes

marks.given: the three nights are written as a made up example

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Take an example. You sleep eight, nine and seven hours on three nights. These numbers are only an example.

beats.on_screen: To find: the average sleep and its boxes on the strip

marks.find: the task is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We find the average sleep, and the boxes it fills on the strip.

marks.add: the three nights are added into one total of twenty four hours

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, add the sleep of all the nights. Eight plus nine plus seven is twenty four hours.

marks.div: the total is divided by the three nights to give eight hours a day

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step two, divide by the number of nights. Twenty four divided by three is eight hours a day.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: boxes = average hours x 2 = 8 x 2

marks.box: two boxes are drawn for each of the eight hours
marks.mul: the working eight times two is written

narration: <bookmark mark='box'/>Step three, each hour is two boxes.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Multiply the eight hours by two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: eight hours of sleep colours 16 boxes; repeat for every activity until 48 boxes are coloured; compare with an adult's strip

marks.sleep: sixteen boxes are coloured as sleep on the strip
marks.rest: the other activities fill the remaining boxes until all forty eight are coloured
marks.adult: an adult's strip is drawn below and the two strips are compared

narration: <bookmark mark='sleep'/>Eight hours of sleep colours sixteen boxes.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Do the same for every activity, until all forty eight boxes are coloured.
<bookmark mark='adult'/>Then track an adult at home, draw their strip, and compare the two.
